Hi Sarah — great question and one we see a lot. TL;DR: yes, marketplace purchases can change the net economics if you try to use the marketplace for both procurement and commit enforcement; however we offer two pragmatic paths and we can lay out the tradeoffs so your finance team can pick what matters most (simplicity vs net effective price). I've attached a one-pager and the tier spreadsheet for illustration.

High-level options (examples use per-token pricing and simplified math):

1) Direct billing + committed tiers (recommended for best net price)
- You sign a revenue commitment (12/24 months) with Redwood and we invoice directly (monthly/quarterly).
- Committed discount applies to all usage billed by Redwood. Example tiers: 0-10M tokens: list price; 10-50M: 12% off; 50-200M: 22% off; 200M+: 30% off (these are example breakpoints, final tiering negotiable).
- No marketplace fees; you get the full committed discount.
- Billing cadence: flexible (monthly invoicing with true-up).

2) Marketplace procurement (procurement prefers single-vendor billing)
- Purchase flows through AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace metering. The marketplace takes a platform fee and remits net to Redwood.
- If you want the committed discount applied at purchase time, we generally need a marketplace-forwarded contract (ISV contract) or a marketplace-managed commitment, which can reduce the net discount because marketplace fees are taken before we apply credits.
- Typical tradeoff: simpler procurement + single PO vs ~5-20% marketplace pass-through that reduces the effective discount (exact share depends on the marketplace and reserved contract terms).

3) Hybrid: commit directly, purchase via marketplace (billing through marketplace, legal through Redwood)
- We can structure a direct commitment (so discount is preserved) while enabling marketplace metering for operational convenience. This requires a brief legal addendum and the marketplace rep to allow pass-through credits. Works well for customers who need marketplace billing for internal chargeback but still want net discounted pricing.

Next steps I propose:
- If you want the cleanest net economics, go direct (option 1). We can draft a 12-month true-up SOW.
- If procurement insists on marketplace-only, we can pull in the AWS rep and a contract specialist and run a quick net-effects calc.

I've attached the "Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v3.pdf" and a draft SOW outline. Jordan / Neha — can one of you run the marketplace net-effect examples (AWS & GCP) and confirm the percent delta on net price after marketplace fees?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman

Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Procurement — looping in Marcus (pricing ops) and Neha (legal) so we can be concrete. Below are two modeled scenarios with numbers you can drop into your TCO model. These are illustrative — final numbers will come from legal/marketplace confirm.

Scenario A — Direct invoice, 12-month commit (best net)
- List per-token: $0.00040 (example)
- Committed tier: 50M tokens/mo average => 22% discount => effective per-token $0.000312
- Billing: monthly invoice with true-up; Redwood absorbs non-marketplace fees.
- Net to Redwood: $0.000312 (no marketplace fees).

Scenario B — AWS Marketplace metered purchase + marketplace-managed commitment
- Marketplace meter sells at list $0.00040 but AWS applies a marketplace platform fee (illustrative 12%) and remits net to Redwood.
- If we attempt to apply a 22% committed discount pre-fee, your net still ends up roughly: 0.00040 * (1 - 0.22) * (1 - 0.12) ≈ $0.000275 net to Redwood, meaning your effective price is lower but the fee wedges the parties and complicates invoicing/credits.
- More commonly, AWS will require the ISV to absorb some marketplace fee or structure the commitment as a separate off-market contract with usage reconciliation; both approaches add administrative steps.

Tradeoffs summarized:
- Direct: slightly higher operational lift for procurement (separate vendor), best net effective price, flexible true-up and credits.
- Marketplace: easier procurement, reduced net to Redwood (marketplace fee), potential restrictions on how discounts are applied and reconciled.

Action items:
- Marcus: can you prepare a concise net-effect calc for AWS/GCP (percent difference vs direct) and flag whether any marketplace programs (private offers, negotiated fees) change the delta?
- Neha: please review the hybrid addendum language we might need to allow marketplace metering + direct commitment.

Sarah / Acadia procurement — if you want, I can schedule a 30-min call with the AWS Marketplace rep and our legal/pricing folks to walk procurement through the exact mechanics.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Deals Manager, Redwood Inference
